matches.title: Solo Molten without Farm or Cowboy.

If I can do it, then so can you, just make sure you have decent towers. Specifically, the Golden Crook Boss or the Accelerator. It doesn't matter just choose what loadout you wish to choose. matches.title: Small Post
matches.snippet: Yeah TDS sucks and there's no point in making this post, but I don't care honestly. I'm not writing this for other people, I'm writing this for myself. Frankly, because I haven't written a long post in such a long time. Tower Defense Simulator is not a game where you strategize (you can but it's not really needed since like everything is soloable), but instead a game full of bugs, lag, horrible balancing, and developers who I think just... don't care about the community! (I mean seriously if they did then why is the game like how it is now) But that's not what I want to talk about. I want to talk about a few towers: the Assassin, the Golden Crook Boss, the Brawler, the Rocketeer, and the Mortar. Before we start. My opinions could be very off and incorrect, because me playing with people is close to zero, due to poor Roblox moderation and everything being soloable. I solo everything and have last played with people during the Ducky Revenge Event. I also don't want to argue with anyone, this is moreso me trying to understand people's views on towers more (because I truly cannot understand them). The first three are the ones I want to compare against. From what I've been seeing, people are saying that the Golden Crook Boss is better... How? Honestly, I played on Simplicity Remaster and the Assassins killed the Fallen Giant on Wave 16 just a little faster than the Golden Crook Boss

matches.title: Fallen Duo+ SPEEDRUN (Personal) Tower Rankings
matches.snippet: Yeah I know. I'm using a tierlist. But I include explanations for each placement, so take this like it's a tower ranking. Essentials You absolutely need these 4 unreplaceable towers when you're speedrunning in Fallen. Period. Commander and DJ are self explanatory Medic to nullify Boomers and Fallen King stuns. Farm can be replaced with Golden Cowboy for the first player, but the the other players need Farm. Best Choices The best towers you can use for speedrunning Fallen, but can be replaced by inferior ones. Gladiator: Carries wave 0 ~ wave 38 since it has high DPS, low cost and infinite AoE. Accelerator: Self explanatory, just extremely high DPS. Engineer: Can be a Sub-DPS, a better choice than Golden Minigunner. Replaceable Towers that are slightly worse than the towers in Best Choices, but by no means bad. Golden Minigunner: High DPS, decent cost. Great for being a Sub-DPS. Decent job as a Main-DPS. Golden Crook Boss: Decent Sub-DPS. Can potentially stop leakings with guards. Ranking is NOT for starting tower. Golden Scout: Great starter tower. Viable Towers that are viable for speedrunning, but there are better options. Sledger: A decent Sub-DPS and minor support for mid to late wave. Turret: Can be used as a Sub-DPS for Trio+. Golden Cowboy: Can only replace farm for the first player, yet is still not the best option to do so. Mediocre Towers that can be used for midrunni

matches.title: why golden crook boss is better than golden scout
matches.snippet: Golden Crook boss and golden scout both have been very good golden skins, up there at the top with mini. But recently, because i have both i wanted to see which one is better and for what reasons. Golden Crook Boss is better than golden scout If you want to see why golden scout is better than golden crook boss, scroll down. it is below and you will see it when you see it, it is in bold. To start, golden crook boss has a higher dps. from when you place it, it can do 2.5 damage per second, while golden scout does 1.33. and when you level it up one time, that damage is doubled and it can one shot everything up to heavy enemies. on the other side, golden scout does 1.33 till level 3, when it does 6.67. At max, golden crook boss does 60 dps to a 20 dps from max golden scout. Golden crook boss also has a faster fire rate, shooting about twice in the time golden scout would shoot until level 3. Continuing, if you farm correctly (6 level 1 farms) you can place a level 3 golden crook boss on wave 10, which effectively buys you a LOT of time to farm (until necromancer i'm pretty sure). On top of that, golden crook boss can summon golden guards, which have 25 health, 25 range, and 6.67 dps, around the same as golden scout at level 3. at max, these guards have more dps than a max golden scout, 33.33 damage, and have 55 health. Why Golden Scout is Better than Golden Crook Boss Golden scout

matches.title: Towers you should get when you are starting out in TDS or you lost your account
matches.snippet: You joined the TDS community recently, and now you can't choose what tower to get. Fear nothing, because this post will help you know what towers to get when you are starting out. Since it is early game, you will of course have the 2 towers: Scout and Sniper. You also start off with some coins, but you should save the coins for later as most of the towers in early game are complete garbage. You should never buy towers that have golden skins (Except for Minigunner and Crook Boss, which is a Level 30 unlockable tower) Your first tower you want to prioritize on getting is Shotgunner. Shotgunner has very high damage on a single shot, reaching over 100+ damage in only 1.5 seconds on max. During the grind for Shotgunner, the only mode you want to play is Molten. No exceptions. Molten is by far the best and the 2nd best for grinding coins and EXP. Molten gives 4x more than Normal and is way easier than Normal mode. When you are ready to start grinding for Shotgunner, do not USE SNIPER. Sniper is overpriced and does the same DPS as Scout, which is way cheaper than Sniper. Because of how terrible Sniper is, you are better off spamming Scouts to deal with the early waves and for the first slow boss. You are unlikely to die on Mystery waves, so do not count on RNG to save you. Once you reach 2500 coins, your next objective is to get Farm. Farm is by far the most required tower in the enti

matches.title: Skills
matches.snippet: I think most Skills are BUNS, and today I'm gonna be making a post talking about all of the current Skills and if I'd use them frequently or not, and if they're good enough to max out or not. OFFENSIVE Firstly, Enhanced Optics. It's good, I like the range buff and it can (obviously) stack with other range buffs, and it's a little bit cheap. Enhanced Optics can sometimes help me catch some leaks sometimes, the only bad thing is it doesn't affect units (I think), and the range buff is pretty low compared to UAV or Easter Egg (although Easter Egg does not always grant Range Buffs), I'll give it a 6/10. Secondly, Improved Gunpowder. It's not great, because I honestly can't find myself caring enough to max it out. I mean the only splash towers I use are Engineer (rarely) and Rocketeer, and honestly, I don't think I need Improved Gunpowder to improve them, it's useless, and to me, a waste of Coins/Skill Credits. 3/10. Thirdly, Fight Dirty. Why would I need this? This is not a good Skill if I'm being honest. It buffs all debuffs, so Pyromancer and all freezing towers, I don't use, Toxic Gunner doesn't need it, and it only slightly benefits Electroshocker, but like if you literally have all 4 (possibly even just 2) Electroshockers placed down, you could just stun lock enemies, as long as they don't have No Stun. Honestly this seems worse than Improved Gunpowder, this is getting a 2/10.

matches.title: Is Golden Scout actually the best obtainable early game tower?
matches.snippet: I've recently unlocked the Golden Scout; naturally, I wanted to try it and use its early game potential in random lobbies. To my surprise, I didn't do too well for the early game. My strategy of course was to spam level 0s, this is because level 1 and 2 only slightly upgrade range and give HD, so spamming level 0s is the most cost efficient early game. I've run into problems with using the tower and I would like to compare it to another tower I have: the Golden Crook Boss. The Golden Crook Boss seems to do better in my experience and here is why: The first upgrade instantly doubles the damage, also one-shotting the quicks (or speedys I always get them confused) The second upgrade gives the golden crook, which is really good for dealing with the heftys on wave 7 and abnormal boss on wave 10 After getting level 2, I'm able to farm and get level 3 for wave 10 even in 4 player servers. Here are things the Golden Scout has going for it Somewhat better range More cost efficient at level 0 Can be placed instantly, unlike the Golden Crook Boss where you need to wait until wave 2 The problem I'm encountering is that by wave 7, Golden Scouts simply won't cut it. Now of course, I can just continue to spam these because of their insane cost-efficiency the moment they are placed, but there are problems with this. The most important issue: Space. matches.title: why I think There is no best golden skin
matches.snippet: Small note: I lost my old account (hihihi99) so this is my new account So you probably hear of golden skins. If you haven't played tds for 2 years or something, golden skins are skins from golden crates that give buffs to towers, like damage. Every golden skin has its unique buff that differs it from the other golden skins and making it better than the original tower. However, you probably also hear of something like this: Golden minigunner is the best golden skin! or Golden soldier is the best golden skin!. Personally, I don't think there is any best golden skin, since there is no golden skin thats amazing at everything and is op from waves 1-40. For example, lets take golden minigunner. Golden minigunner might be a good mid-late game tower, but im pretty sure you can't get it on wave 1 and you will have to leak alot and maybe even die before affording it. Another example could be golden scout. It does excel at wave 1-9, but golden scout is never going to be able to handle the last waves of fallen mode unless you spam it real bad until the placement limit and then fallen king comes and wrecks you on the last wave instead. In conclusion, every golden skin is good at its own thing (yes even golden pyromancer since he can reduce defense of enemies on fallen mode) and there isn't really a best golden skin unless your talking of the best golden skin in a very specific scenario. TL;DR nerf Golden Scout and buff Military Base, Crook Boss, Shotgunner, and Ace so all 5 can be on the same level. So basically, Golden towers are the most expensive. But were they designed to be the best at it's job? No! They were designed to be the 2nd best at their job, like a fun golden tower but not an OP one. Golden Minigunner, Golden Pyromancer, and Golden Cowboy are all good examples of this, being outclassed by the late game alliance(Ranger, Accel, Engineer), Mortar, and Farm respectively. Golden Crook Boss and Golden Soldier on the other hand, are outclassed by a literal Golden tower. This guy is Golden Scout. I am ok with it's OP early game if it's outclassed by a tower you get earlier on, but it deals 36 DPS at max level and can solo fallen with supports. What the fuck. This tower should only do something like 20-25 DPS at max, it's not supposed to be good for the mid game. It might need an early game price nerf, but if I say such shit, everyone is gonna scream. Why not nerf Gladiator, rebalance Ace to be more early game oriented, and buff Crook Boss, make Shotgunner's spread tighter on level 0, and clean up Military Base, in which these towers are the early game towers people use

matches.title: Accelerator needs a gimmick
matches.snippet: Accelerator is in a very weird spot where people want it to be good, but not too good to the point it outclasses every other DPS option again. But now we're in this place where everything is arguably better than accelerator, such as Turret, Pursuit, Brawler, Engineer, Golden Minigunner and Golden Crook Boss. There is reasons why people deem these towers "better than accelerator.' The Reasons Golden Minigunner and Turret having consistent DPS, allowing them to be buffed from support towers. Pursuit and Brawler being able to traverse the map, effectively allowing them to always be attacking something. Engineer and Golden Crook Boss for cost efficiency and the ability to summon units, with the downside of unable to buff units but having good to decent DPS from the tower itself. Meanwhile the Accelerator's gimmick is that it has a windup and cooldown after attacking, which serves no benefit really other than to cripple Accelerator for game balancing reasons. The Changes Instead of this weird ammo-like gimmick it has where damage buffs and fire rate buffs makes the overcharge go up quicker, it should be instead a timer where accelerator has a few seconds before going into cooldown. This means damage buffs and firerate buffs don't make the overcharge quicker, but instead make great use of the limited time accelerator has. Another change is changing the size of the footprint from 1.5

matches.snippet: Part 26 of the Historical Tower Ranking Read Part 1 for more info: https://tds.fandom.com/f/p/4400000000000287719/r/4400000000001741834 We're now diving into Overhaul v1.3, the Frost Invasion Update. This update came out SIX MONTHS after the “Halloween” “2020” Update on May 8th, 2021. This update brought about two new towers, lots of patch notes, the Frost Invasion Event and unfortunately, more bugs and another long time span of no updates. MISCALLENOUS CHANGES Defense Rework - Defense was now changed to drop damage by a percentage instead of dropping it by a specific number based on the gamemode multiplier. This change made it so high burst damage towers, such as Ranger no longer had an advantage. It still stayed in the meta though. The defense dropping towers (Pyromancer, Electroshocker, Freezer, Frost Blaster) were also now more effective on dropping defense, since they also now dropped defense by a percentage. Splash Damage Rework - The explosion is now separated into two spheres, with the inner sphere dealing 100% of the stated damage while the outer sphere decreases damage linearly. This is nice, as towers dealing splash damage are now more consistent. Unfortunately, with the state of balancing of the game, almost every splash tower is very weak. He continued to go into matches and won easily. Until… Blox’s soul was sucked into the game. However, he didn’t notice and continued to play. Eventually, his soul was split into small pieces. His heart was beating out of his chest. “W-what?! Why can’t I.. what is going on?!? Am I… IN THE GAME?!?” Meanwhile, the towers were having fun in the Inventory with their newfound ability to move. “Hey guys.. what is that?”, said Commander. He was pointing at a bright door in the center of the Inventory. “Who’s gonna go through it?”, said Scout. “Three… two.. one.. NOT IT!!”, they all said at the same time. Honestly, I played on Simplicity Remaster and the Assassins killed the Fallen Giant on Wave 16 just a little faster than the Golden Crook Boss

Frankly, because I haven't written a long post in such a long time. Tower Defense Simulator is not a game where you strategize (you can but it's not really needed since like everything is soloable), but instead a game full of bugs, lag, horrible balancing, and developers who I think just... don't care about the community! (I mean seriously if they did then why is the game like how it is now) But that's not what I want to talk about. I want to talk about a few towers: the Assassin, the Golden Crook Boss, the Brawler, the Rocketeer, and the Mortar. Before we start. My opinions could be very off and incorrect, because me playing with people is close to zero, due to poor Roblox moderation and everything being soloable. I solo everything and have last played with people during the Ducky Revenge Event. I also don't want to argue with anyone, this is moreso me trying to understand people's views on towers more (because I truly cannot understand them). The first three are the ones I want to compare against. From what I've been seeing, people are saying that the Golden Crook Boss is better... How? Honestly, I played on Simplicity Remaster and the Assassins killed the Fallen Giant on Wave 16 just a little faster than the Golden Crook Boss. The Golden Crook Boss's units, at least to me, are frankly useless. The only Tower I like to use that has units I actually like is the Mercenary Base. Speaking about that, the Mercenary Base may or may not take shorter to grind for than the Golden Crook Boss, though I'm unsure, as I'm way past Level 150 and have all Golden Towers so... I can't confirm anything. What's so good about the Golden Crook Boss? Now I got a reply to a comment I made on the Golden Crook Boss page where somebody straight up just insulted me for no reason (wasn't even talking about the tower itself I was joking about the image in the infobox). You can view the image below: Firstly, I just wanna say that I don't see the Golden Crook Boss seen in the TDS videos I've seen (nor the Assassin but I have seen the Brawler used sometimes), but I barely watch TDS, since most content not made by the Platter Bros or like propellars or CORSO is boring. Secondly, I wanna say that the Golden Crook Boss, from what I've seen, kind of falls off in Late Game. Thirdly, you know who else has good cost efficiency? The Assassin. With $59.15 COST EFFICIENCY AT MAX LEVEL!!! You hear how crazy that sounds?! 59!!! Fourthly, many towers have Hidden Detection so that point is redundant, and the Flying Detection is kind of just... bad. I mean you got the Ranger, the Gatling Gun (which I wouldn't recommend using but still), the Electroshocker, the Commander, the Mercenary Base, the Necromancer, and other towers I think are better with Flying Detection. Lastly, no. I am not ragebaiting. I have like... never rage baited. Please don't try to argue with me and scream at me saying the Golden Crook Boss is good. Unless I get points better than THAT on how the Golden Crook Boss is like apparently outstanding or whatever, yeah, I'm sticking to my Archer, Assassin, Golden Cowboy, and other towers. Oh yeah, also, the Golden Cowboy can give you money... Golden Crook Boss can't. Oh well, yeah, the only good Golden Tower is the Golden Cowboy (maybe the Golden Minigunner too?). Next, I wanna ask a question. Were the balancers taking the Brawler into account when buffing the Assassin? Yeah, the Assassin has 40 less DPS. Except there's one problem... The Brawler has a Placement Limit of 6. The Assassin? None! No Placement Limit! Nada! Mind you, the Brawler takes like 4 games of the objectively 2nd most boring gamemode in the entire game (right behind PvP). The Assassin? Oh yeah, it only takes 3 games of Easy mode, 2 games of Casual, Intermediate, and Molten, and 1 game of Fallen. What the hell? Should've only gotten a small buff on Level 0 to be able to get past Wave 1 in Fallen, but that's it. This buff is WAY too big. I hope the Assassin gets nerfed in the next update. Because if I had to choose between the Assassin or the Brawler... I'm going for the Assassin. I will say this. The PvP stats for these towers are pretty good. They should be transferred over to the regular game, as I think this is good balancing. Though! I've used neither towers in PvP, sooo... I might be a little lost on this. Yes, the Brawler can knockback. Yes, the Brawler can reposition. Yes, he has good stats. But like... why would I use him over the Assassin, who can literally clear out the entirety of Fallen mode (possibly) up to Wave 22 with the Fallen Seraphs? Can the Brawler do that? I have no clue! I haven't tried it yet! But if I had to guess, probably not, since he's kind of expensive compared to the Assassin, costing $10,250 more to max out. Small section to ask, why can the Militant make it to Wave 40 in Fallen? I did lose,

verified_top_matches.snippet: this will probably be the last tier list i ever make, honestly. reasoning provided for all towers for once. every placement primarily assumes viability in the lategame content, such as special maps and hardcore. TIERS ARE NOT ORDERED Scout: D. Sees very little usage past Easy and Casual and is almost always dead weight. Somehow still capable of somewhat functioning in Frost though (source: matchmaking teammates), so escapes F. Golden Scout: A. One of the few actual earlygame specialists in the entire game, and honestly the only good one. Curbstomps just about every mode, though past Wave 19 he loses almost all of his utility. Sniper: Honestly, F. Completely outclassed even if he apparently somehow works as Hardcore earlygame. No reason to ever use him, even Slime Trooper is better. What a joke of a tower. Paintballer: D. Considered C, but due to recently gained niche overlap with Demoman also losing his damage falloff, there's basically no reason to use Paintballer anymore beyond "haha funny". Demoman: G.Demo exists, condemned to D tier. Designed to be outclassed. Golden Demoman: A. Sweeps Hardcore and various other modes, popping off most in duos. A bit heavy on placement, but insane CE for an AoE tower and the lack of falloff greatly bump it up. Boomerang: I have no idea, I have literally never even touched this tower. It looks good statwise but I doubt it sees much usage any

A bit heavy on placement, but insane CE for an AoE tower and the lack of falloff greatly bump it up. Boomerang: I have no idea, I have literally never even touched this tower. It looks good statwise but I doubt it sees much usage anywhere past like, Molten. Weird choice of detections too, but I suppose it improves Hardcore viability. Slime Trooper: B. The only actually decent starter tower. Max level AoE is nice and slowdown is pretty welcome, plus his cost efficiency isn't half bad for what he does. Still outclassed pretty hard by Hacker, but far less expensive to make up for it. Also a direct upgrade to Sniper. Soldier: C. Tower that exists. Functional DPS early on but may as well be a joke tower past Intermediate. Golden Soldier: B. Potential man and whatnot, but on a less ironic end, G.Soldier is just totally outclassed in every regard. Earlygame? Golden Scout exists and so does Engineer. Midgame? Crook Boss. Just use Crook Boss. Lategame? What the fuck are you thinking? If anything, at least he still has usable stats. Just use G.Mini if you need a spammable DPS as well. Shotgunner: A, but honestly close to S. The upscale is crazy with this tower, and it just shreds almost every mode in the entire game. Absolutely ridiculous how this got through playtesting, even Hardcore is fodderized. Freezer: Another A tier. Pretty much the only real source of freeze that both isn't completely outclassed and isn't named Frost Blaster. Very accessible, very powerful. Assassin: C. Literally why ever use this tower when Brawler exists, and why ever use Brawler when Golden Scout exists. They could at least give him lead... Militant: B. Slightly worse Golden Soldier except its not 50,000 coins. Accessible and somewhat reliable, but... just use anyone else past Frost mode. Hunter: B. Possibly controversial take, but Hunter honestly isn't half bad. Unfortunately for him, though, he runs into major niche overlap with Ranger and since everyone and their grandma has a shitload of range nowadays, his range niche may as well not exist. Sniper is also crying to himself yet again. Pyromancer: B. This tower like, exists, I guess. It's just worse G.Pyro. Still works in Hardcore somehow. Golden Pyromancer: Also B. Hardcore/Voidcore earlygame merchant and that's basically where his viability ends. Truly, a tower. Ace Pilot: I'll admit, I haven't used this tower in a good while. From the looks of it though, Ace is still a CE merchant. Inconsistent, but the godly cost efficiency makes up for it. I'll put him in B just to be safe, but know that he'd be very close to A tier. Medic: S is for Support. On a less silly end, Medic is like, really good in Hardcore and Voidcore. That and a 5.4k DPS Juggernaut is ridiculous. Farm: The S in Farm stands for Shit. In other words, literally essential, what are you doing if you aren't using this tower in Hardcore/Voidcore. Not as versatile elsewhere, but the only mode you actively don't want Farm in is Polluted Wasteland, better known as the most braindead shit ever. Literal loadout simulator of a mode. Electroshocker: B. Nerf was admittedly somewhat justified, but like... come on, dude, Tesla is still straight dogshit. Lategame viability has sadly been hit pretty hard, but at least he hits some good earlygame damage thresholds. Rocketeer: Into the A tier bucket. I shouldn't have to explain why the strong AoE tower with no damage falloff is good. Trapper: I'm very contested on Trapper, but I think B is the best spot for him. Great at what he does, but what he does isn't really super valuable. Beartraps are admittedly really good, though. Also works in PW2 somehow. Military Base: B, definition of decent. Simply fell off over time with the absurd stat inflation accelerated by Shock & Awe. Also can't even slightly work earlygame anymore... Crook Boss: Another

verified_top_matches.title: why golden crook boss is better than golden scout
verified_top_matches.snippet: Golden Crook boss and golden scout both have been very good golden skins, up there at the top with mini. But recently, because i have both i wanted to see which one is better and for what reasons. Golden Crook Boss is better than golden scout If you want to see why golden scout is better than golden crook boss, scroll down. it is below and you will see it when you see it, it is in bold. To start, golden crook boss has a higher dps. from when you place it, it can do 2.5 damage per second, while golden scout does 1.33. and when you level it up one time, that damage is doubled and it can one shot everything up to heavy enemies. on the other side, golden scout does 1.33 till level 3, when it does 6.67. At max, golden crook boss does 60 dps to a 20 dps from max golden scout. Golden crook boss also has a faster fire rate, shooting about twice in the time golden scout would shoot until level 3. Continuing, if you farm correctly (6 level 1 farms) you can place a level 3 golden crook boss on wave 10, which effectively buys you a LOT of time to farm (until necromancer i'm pretty sure). On top of that, golden crook boss can summon golden guards, which have 25 health, 25 range, and 6.67 dps, around the same as golden scout at level 3. at max, these guards have more dps than a max golden scout, 33.33 damage, and have 55 health. Obviously, this is just on paper, and the units can easily be wiped out in late-game. When you are ready to start grinding for Shotgunner, do not USE SNIPER. Sniper is overpriced and does the same DPS as Scout, which is way cheaper than Sniper. Because of how terrible Sniper is, you are better off spamming Scouts to deal with the early waves and for the first slow boss. You are unlikely to die on Mystery waves, so do not count on RNG to save you. Once you reach 2500 coins, your next objective is to get Farm. Farm is by far the most required tower in the entire game (Events do not give any money, so do not bring it when you are doing events), being more useful than Cowboy. Since you have Shotgunner, grinding will be much easier, as you can reach Wave 40 if you get enough Shotgunners to deal with the zombies. Once you get Farm, your next objective is to get Dj Booth and Commander. This will allow you to solo Molten with no problem, which makes it so that once you reach the Molten Boss, you will not have to micro your towers to the back. Getting Commander and Dj Booth will not be as simple, as you will have to get them in 3+ hours since they cost 7500 if combined. Once you get Commander and Dj Booth, you will enter the middle game, where you will have to start grinding for levels and coins. During this time, you should get Ranger, Military Base, Minigunner, Turret and Ace Pilot. This will allow you to prepare for Hardcore, which is required for grinding Accelerator and completing the mode itself. During the grinding, the towers you want to get first will be listed in an order, with one being the first should be priortized first. Ranger Golden Crook Boss > Golden Scout > Golden Cowboy > Golden Pyromancer > Golden Soldier. Once you get Golden Minigunner, Golden Scout and Golden Crook Boss, do not grind for the last golden crates. They are not worth it unless you are doing challenges. After you have finished the entire game, you are in the End game, where you can carry noobs, do events, keep up with the community and just help others, and etc. IF this guide helped you, please comment. This post took over an hour to write. In a nutshell, you should get Shotgunner as your first tower, Farm, Supports, essential towers for triumphing Hardcore, Accelerator, events, Hidden Wave Badge, Pursuit, and Golden Crates. verified_top_matches.snippet: I think most Skills are BUNS, and today I'm gonna be making a post talking about all of the current Skills and if I'd use them frequently or not, and if they're good enough to max out or not. OFFENSIVE Firstly, Enhanced Optics. It's good, I like the range buff and it can (obviously) stack with other range buffs, and it's a little bit cheap. Enhanced Optics can sometimes help me catch some leaks sometimes, the only bad thing is it doesn't affect units (I think), and the range buff is pretty low compared to UAV or Easter Egg (although Easter Egg does not always grant Range Buffs), I'll give it a 6/10. Secondly, Improved Gunpowder. It's not great, because I honestly can't find myself caring enough to max it out. I mean the only splash towers I use are Engineer (rarely) and Rocketeer, and honestly, I don't think I need Improved Gunpowder to improve them, it's useless, and to me, a waste of Coins/Skill Credits. 3/10. Thirdly, Fight Dirty. Why would I need this? This is not a good Skill if I'm being honest. It buffs all debuffs, so Pyromancer and all freezing towers, I don't use, Toxic Gunner doesn't need it, and it only slightly benefits Electroshocker, but like if you literally have all 4 (possibly even just 2) Electroshockers placed down, you could just stun lock enemies, as long as they don't have No Stun. Honestly this seems worse than Improved Gunpowder, this is getting a 2/10.

Pretty good splash damage tower, but HD is still a problem because it's locked away at max level. Hunter: Basically a sniper on the ground. No point in using it though because the ground is usually where higher DPS towers are placed, and it sorta just wastes space for those towers. However, it is a pretty good fly-detection tower and when spammed, it destroys swarms of weak enemies. Soldier: Really good tower for early game because of its high burst of damage. It can solo Easy Mode on Crossroads/Rocket Arena and overall is the best Starter tower. But in late game, the soldier quickly becomes useless as higher-health enemies come in. INTERMEDIATE TOWERS Militant: With support towers, some farms to get the upgrades quick, and an early-game defender, the Militant can beat Molten Mode on most maps. Its a more spammable, alternative version to the Minigunner, and overall is really good. It also has fly detection and hidden detection, so its high damage output and spammability can make it a good early-game hardcore tower, taking down even a mega slow when enough are placed down. Medic: Underrated. The Medic, being bad at easier gamemodes, is ESSENTIAL for harder ones, where you're getting stunned left, right and center. The stun cleansing allows for quick recovery and maximizes damage dealt to the boss, and with your steady stream of cash, level 5 medics will not be a problem to spam. Freezer: Ever since the rework, the Freezer is just a scout/soldier that slows down enemies. Pretty decent option when you need to slow enemies, but honestly just get an electroshocker. Farm: What more can I say? It's the farm. Its a great option that provides HEAVY doses of cash at the end of the wave, allowing you to get stronger towers quicker. Essential for your game. Shotgunner: When you need to speed past the early rounds, shotgunner is here! The shotgunner is a spammable tower that honestly acts more like a melee option, meaning that it has low range and high damage. Using this on a map like Crossroads or Rocket Arena on Easy/Molten/Intermediate allows you to SPEED past the early game. Sometimes the boss health bars even flash red when it shoots. However, after each enemy debut, the shotgunner slowly and slowly becomes less useful in your run, so you should probably sell them later on. Rocketeer: The hunter version of the Mortar, the Rocketeer offers high damage with splash at a slow fire rate. Its decent, but the deadzone can be a problem even if you place it far from the path. I don't see myself using this. Trapper: Can help you catch leaks from weak enemies, but you really must be a master of placement to make this work. Late game enemies also are super strong and can probably just plow through the traps, so be careful when using it. Super bad on tracks with multiple lanes. Ace Pilot: The main use for this is hardcore, but I do see it being used in maps such as Pizza Party to counter Balloon Kids. However it's generally better to bring other towers with higher DPS to your game, but this is a good tower. You can also place it near your rangers to give them HD for a while, and using this strat I soloed Molten on Wrecked. Pyromancer: good for EARLY EARLY game and against invisibles when level 2, but the fact that i cant be bothered to even have correct grammar definitely says something. defense melting can be useful though. Military Base: Solid tower with many upsides. It can also clutch your run when some unit spawns when you're about to lose. Absolute chad tower, but be sure to get Mounted Gunners as soon as possible. Crook Boss: This tower is just Military Base but the tower itself shoots at enemies. The goons the Crook Boss summons stop walking when shooting, so they can stack up to deal massive damage, but I don't use it enough to be talking. ADVANCED TOWERS Electroshocker: High damage along with stuns make this tower really good. However a LOT of zombies have stun immunity, so it has a sort-of shotgunner situation, where it becomes worse with every wave passed. Also the placement limit of 4 really brings it down. They'd have well-upgraded towers[if solo], or massive numbers of decent-damage dealing towers[not solo] so they'd be killed quite easily considering there's more options and towers are more balanced, allowing for more options if you must face obstacles provided by enemies. In early game, they aren't an issue[worst case scenario.] In late game, they mostly spammed Giant Bosses[Now Giant Fallens], so it isn't much of an issue as it was back then. There were a couple outliers but hardly anyone died, nor will it change now. Regarding "strategy," they're used to plan for the unexpected and to defeat the enemy. It isn't "follow this google doc/map, if something goes wrong we all die." Strategies should be flexible and be open to variability, not set-in stone and nothing can change or else you lose. Set targeting wrong? Lose. Delayed by a wave? Lose. Placement 3 studs off? Lose. An enemy has 10 more hp than anticipated? Lose. You get the point. 2. EXPERIMENT[SANDBOX] - This experiment will be early game, and it'll be using: golden CB, brawler, golden so. These towers were chosen as I see people using these in early game the most, and also in solo games. 5 Mystery[worst case scenario, 5 abnormal bosses] 2 lvl. 2 Golden CB: effectively killed all abnormal bosses 4 lvl. 2 Golden So: effectively killed all abnormal bosses 2 lvl. 3 Brawler: effectively killed all abnormal bosses 5 Breaker[2]: 2 lvl. 2 Golden CB: Annihilated the breakers with [a bit of struggle compared to the other 2] ease 4 lvl. 2 Golden So: Annihilated the breakers with ease 2 lvl. 3 Brawler: Annihilated the breakers with ease I felt a bit generous, experimenting w/ 5 Breaker 3: 2 lvl. 3 Brawler: Leaked 1 max-hp breaker3 & 2 4 lvl. 2 Golden So: Leaked 1 10 hp breaker3 & max-hp breaker2 These early game towers faired well against a Breaker 3, a more mid-game enemy. What does this say about Breaker? It's fairly easy to kill and makes the game easier, as compared to Mystery which poses challenges but's still possible to defeat[if you somehow let mysteries get so close to the base then spawn a massive enemy, you'd probably have died to another enemy that same wave or died later on.] 3. MODERN RNG & WHATABOUTISM Typically, people point fingers to "jester," or "slime." Slime has 100-115 HP depending on the scaling, and I've seen some people complain it spawned into something like tank or some other enemy[on this wiki, discord, and in the lobby]. Do you see that "100-115 hp" part? Right, so explain how you even let it slip by to get close enough to the base or let it live long enough to transform? Fallen Jester shouldn't even be an issue anyways unless you're "grahhhh dps" monkey. The HP ranges from 800-970[it debuts on wave 19], and most people don't even complain about it mid-game, nor do I see it presenting issues during that time. It's late game when it becomes more of a problem due to more enemy spam & higher-hp enemies. However, one word. Electroshocker. To my surprise, I didn't do too well for the early game. My strategy of course was to spam level 0s, this is because level 1 and 2 only slightly upgrade range and give HD, so spamming level 0s is the most cost efficient early game. I've run into problems with using the tower and I would like to compare it to another tower I have: the Golden Crook Boss. The Golden Crook Boss seems to do better in my experience and here is why: The first upgrade instantly doubles the damage, also one-shotting the quicks (or speedys I always get them confused) The second upgrade gives the golden crook, which is really good for dealing with the heftys on wave 7 and abnormal boss on wave 10 After getting level 2, I'm able to farm and get level 3 for wave 10 even in 4 player servers. Here are things the Golden Scout has going for it Somewhat better range More cost efficient at level 0 Can be placed instantly, unlike the Golden Crook Boss where you need to wait until wave 2 The problem I'm encountering is that by wave 7, Golden Scouts simply won't cut it. Now of course, I can just continue to spam these because of their insane cost-efficiency the moment they are placed, but there are problems with this. The most important issue: Space. Golden Scouts do have more range and more cost efficient DPS counting out the crooks and mafia of the Golden Crook Boss, but you can't just place all of them in the exact same optimal spot. Inevitably, some of them are going to have much worse range coverage than others placed in the same spot like the 3-4 turn coverage on Harbor Even with a decent amount of level 0s placed, they can't seem to deal with the heftys on wave 7 very well, and if I try to upgrade one for better damage I actually let a couple of enemies leak, especially on maps that don't have great spots to get optimal range coverage. The damage isn't a big deal, but keep in mind I want a good early game tower and the Golden Crook Boss only requires I leak on wave 1-3 depending on the amount of players (less income) and map. I don't see the Golden Crook Boss used for many strats, as the Golden Scout is a decently popular hidden wave tower, but the Golden Scout seems to only be good under heavily controlled circumstances, maybe even more so than the Swarmer. I want towers that can be good for the role I want it to do under almost any circumstances, but it seems the Golden Scout is only good if I get a highly optimal map and I pray that a teammate can place something good for wave 10. You can say it's just because I play with randoms, so on a true tier list Golden Scout might still be pretty high, but this just seems to be another scenario where a tower is worse on wifi due to certain mechanics like less income, less total towers for each player and the obvious fact that I'm not playing with experienced players, but most of my games of TDS are obviously not gonna be with professionals. So yes, to my surprise, I am somewhat disappointed by the Golden Scout. If I'm just using it wrong on wifi then let me know. verified_top_matches.title: why I think There is no best golden skin
verified_top_matches.snippet: Small note: I lost my old account (hihihi99) so this is my new account So you probably hear of golden skins. If you haven't played tds for 2 years or something, golden skins are skins from golden crates that give buffs to towers, like damage. Every golden skin has its unique buff that differs it from the other golden skins and making it better than the original tower. However, you probably also hear of something like this: Golden minigunner is the best golden skin! or Golden soldier is the best golden skin!. Personally, I don't think there is any best golden skin, since there is no golden skin thats amazing at everything and is op from waves 1-40. For example, lets take golden minigunner. Golden minigunner might be a good mid-late game tower, but im pretty sure you can't get it on wave 1 and you will have to leak alot and maybe even die before affording it. Another example could be golden scout. It does excel at wave 1-9, but golden scout is never going to be able to handle the last waves of fallen mode unless you spam it real bad until the placement limit and then fallen king comes and wrecks you on the last wave instead. In conclusion, every golden skin is good at its own thing (yes even golden pyromancer since he can reduce defense of enemies on fallen mode) and there isn't really a best golden skin unless your talking of the best golden skin in a very specific scenario. So for those who dont know, Golden Perks are the things that comes with Golden Skins. By activating this, you can use any other skin you want without losing the Golden Perks. Say goodbye to being stuck with only Golden Scout with his Deagle, and say hello to the Eclipse Scout with his dope Mauser. Also, with the Golden Perk update, there comes Golden Towers rework. They should be considered as individual towers now. Welp, time to do a quick review on the towers i own Golden Scout The GS, before this update, is one one the best Early Game tower for speedrunning. And in this update, it got a buff, making it even better. Golden Cowboy This tower, before the update, can be used as a replacement for Farm, but its usage is limited to Solo, a bit useful on Duo, but other than that... meh Now, with this update, it might be useable for Duos, i guess. Idk, i dont use this tower much tbh. Golden Crook Boss So basically the GCB got a buff this update. To start off, the tower now cost 600$ to place and deal 3 damage at lv 0, which make it so that you can place it at wave 0, making it a good early defend tower. Its price on lower levels got increased, and the minion stats got nerfed, making it worse for mid game, however, its last level damage got buffed, making it basically a cheaper and better Minigunner, with 4 placement limit. Golden Pyro One of the greatest anime comeback ever. The Golden Pyro, once the worst Golden Tower in the game, now turned into one of the best. GP's DPS is quite good for Early Game, with the ability to pierce, making it a great option for Early Game. Its Defense Melting is also good for Late Game, to deal with Fallen Guardians, and its ability to have HD at Lv0 makes it so that you would be considered "sane" if you bring this to Hardcore. New Tower Finally, after what feels like 2 years (Oh wait, lemme check....) Yeah, its around 2 years, we have a new Hardcore tower: the Engineer. Wait WHAT? 4500 GEMS? THAT IS RIDICULOUS Thats might be what some people (including me) think when the Engineer was released. I mean, like, cmon, the Accelerator was such a pain in the ass to grind, now THIS? Even if they buffed the HC win prize, not many people can find a good team to win it (before you say "Discord", i dont think that most TDS player are old enough to use Discord legally) As time pass by, however, i realized that, well, without Engineer, my life is.... fine. Birds still singing, flowers still blooming, i still cant beat Touhou 8 on Normal without using any continues (f### you Marisa Kirisame, stop stealing my lives and bombs, i need those for Stage 5 and 6 because Reisen keep on beating my ass) and Necrofantasia still slaps. I mean, like, even without Engineer, Accelerator is still a good tower. And for those who complains that the Engineer might cost 24-25 hours to grind, well..., just dont do it continiously. Enginner isnt going anywhere, take your time. When you feel too bored from grinding, just... take a break, go play something else, and come back when you are ready to grind again. And well, if you dont have time for TDS, well, just do 1,2 Hardcore matches per day. Like i said, Engineer isnt going anywhere, you got all the time on the world to get the tower. Overall, i find that Enginner's addition is a good addition to the game, for those who are truly determined. You dont have to get that tower, not early. You can just get Accel or GMini and its fine enough. Suddenly, the map started to darken. Scout walked through the exit, leaving the two towers behind, and returned to Ness’ inventory. He saw a bright, white door in the distance. He decided to go through it and ended up in the Lobby. “What is this place?”, said Scout. “The lobby.”, said Ness. “Also thanks for helping scare away those toxic players back there. We’ll always be together until the end, I promise!” And so, the two of them triumphed on many maps. Scout even made some new friends like Demoman, Freezer, Commander, and Crook Boss. A few weeks later, Ness was already a level 66 and had enough coins to buy his first golden crate. His loadout at the time was Turret, Farm, Commander, Enforcer, and then there was Scout. However, he didn’t know what to replace with Golden Minigunner. He thought his loadout was close to perfection, but then he decided to replace Scout with Golden Mini. Scout fell back into the dark void known as the inventory. Soon, his old friends found him on the dusty ground, lying there. “Dam, you got replaced?”, said Freezer while helping Scout get up. “You two were inseparable!” “He broke a promise. He killed them out of pure anger. He was replaced by Minigunner, one of the towers that taunted him the first time Ness played. Freezer was on the floor, playing dead. Scout walked through the door that led to the lobby. He stayed near the MEGA Servers section of the lobby, until.. “Hey, what’re you doing here all by yourself, little fella?”, said a dark figure. They had a burger on their head. “Dont talk to me.” “Oh, my bad! Looks like you’re not really too fond of other people, or am I wrong?” “My player left me for a Golden Minigunner.” “Well, that must suck! Anyways, I’m a part of a secret organization. Our goal? DESTROY THIS GAME. How’re we gonna do that? By completely destroying players! Why not nerf Gladiator, rebalance Ace to be more early game oriented, and buff Crook Boss, make Shotgunner's spread tighter on level 0, and clean up Military Base, in which these towers are the early game towers people use

verified_top_matches.title: Accelerator needs a gimmick
verified_top_matches.snippet: Accelerator is in a very weird spot where people want it to be good, but not too good to the point it outclasses every other DPS option again. But now we're in this place where everything is arguably better than accelerator, such as Turret, Pursuit, Brawler, Engineer, Golden Minigunner and Golden Crook Boss. There is reasons why people deem these towers "better than accelerator.' The Reasons Golden Minigunner and Turret having consistent DPS, allowing them to be buffed from support towers. Pursuit and Brawler being able to traverse the map, effectively allowing them to always be attacking something. Engineer and Golden Crook Boss for cost efficiency and the ability to summon units, with the downside of unable to buff units but having good to decent DPS from the tower itself. Meanwhile the Accelerator's gimmick is that it has a windup and cooldown after attacking, which serves no benefit really other than to cripple Accelerator for game balancing reasons. The Changes Instead of this weird ammo-like gimmick it has where damage buffs and fire rate buffs makes the overcharge go up quicker, it should be instead a timer where accelerator has a few seconds before going into cooldown. This means damage buffs and firerate buffs don't make the overcharge quicker, but instead make great use of the limited time accelerator has. Another change is changing the size of the footprint from 1.5

verified_top_matches.full_thread_text_excerpt: Part 26 of the Historical Tower Ranking Read Part 1 for more info: https://tds.fandom.com/f/p/4400000000000287719/r/4400000000001741834 We're now diving into Overhaul v1.3, the Frost Invasion Update. This update came out SIX MONTHS after the “Halloween” “2020” Update on May 8th, 2021. This update brought about two new towers, lots of patch notes, the Frost Invasion Event and unfortunately, more bugs and another long time span of no updates. MISCALLENOUS CHANGES Defense Rework - Defense was now changed to drop damage by a percentage instead of dropping it by a specific number based on the gamemode multiplier. This change made it so high burst damage towers, such as Ranger no longer had an advantage. It still stayed in the meta though. The defense dropping towers (Pyromancer, Electroshocker, Freezer, Frost Blaster) were also now more effective on dropping defense, since they also now dropped defense by a percentage. Splash Damage Rework - The explosion is now separated into two spheres, with the inner sphere dealing 100% of the stated damage while the outer sphere decreases damage linearly. This is nice, as towers dealing splash damage are now more consistent. Unfortunately, with the state of balancing of the game, almost every splash tower is very weak. NEW TOWERS Toxic Gunner - Unlocked from beating the “Halloween” “2020” Event, the Toxic Gunner fired in bursts, similar to the Soldier. These shots apply slowdown to enemies, while also dealing damage over time. However, it was extremely buggy on release. The slowdown was PERMANENT. Every enemy hit would be slowed down by FIFTY PERCENT, and best of all, the slowdown affected MAJOR BOSSES such as Void Reaver, Frost Spirit and Creator.. Really, the only problem Toxic Gunner had was no hidden detection, which barely matters when you make every game a free win. It was the main reason why the Frost Invasion Event was so easy to win, contrary to what the developers stated (in fact it made the event soloable). Toxic Gunner easily lands on S tier, #1. It was really that broken. How did this get past testing? Sledger - Unlocked from beating the Frost Invasion Event, the Sledger was another melee tower, attacking enemies by bashing them with its hammer. These swings could miss enemies and only hit one target, so Sledger wasn’t that good at early game. Level 3+ is when things get good. It is now able to freeze targets, multiple of them. The freeze time was always 2 seconds, not restricted by enemy size unlike Freezer and Frost Blaster. At Level 4+, frozen enemies would receive twice the damage, so Sledger was actually pretty good at defending by itself, being excellent at crowd control, and it is just much more effective at actually freezing enemies than Freezer or Frost Blaster ever could, so it was a very vital tower for Hidden Wave. Really, the only thing Sledger struggled against were hidden enemies as it didn’t have hidden detection, major bosses, which was made worse by Sledger’s low placement limit of six. It lands a spot on high A tier. BALANCE CHANGES Freezer Level 3 Defense dropping: 1 -> 5% Level 5 Defense dropping: 2 -> 10% Frost Blaster Level 3 Defense dropping: 1 -> 5% Just the global change every tower with this ability got. Both towers still suck I fear. They remain in E tier. Militant Militant now has ammo, when it runs out of ammo, or does not detect any enemies for a while, it will start reloading. Level 0 Cost: $1,200 -> 750 Damage: 2 -> 1 Firerate: 0.43s -> 0.23s Range: 12 -> 10 Now has 18 ammo, Reload Time of 2.5s Level 1 Damage: 2 -> 1 Firerate: 0.43s -> 0.23s Range: 14 -> 12 Level 2 Damage: 2 -> 1 Firerate: 0.43s -> 0.23s Range: 15 -> 13 Level 3 Damage remains at 2 Firerate: 0.23s -> 0.155s Range: 15 -> 13 Now has 30 ammo Level 4 Damage remains at 4 Firerate: 0.23s -> 0.155s Range: 15 -> 14 Level 5 removed The developers said this would make Militant “better”. Guess what? It did the exact opposite. The ammo system just doesn’t work and is such a HUGE hindrance, especially now that the tower’s range was even worse, and the reload time of 2.5s is just miserable. The DPS is already too little for its cost, except for Level 0. The DPS was literally LESS than Medic’s, a support tower. Militant goes down from low C tier to E tier, now among one of the worst towers in the game. Medic Level 5 BUG: Cleansing ability no longer removes stuns from towers, due to the new stun system. Well, guess what. Medic’s main use is basically redundant now. While it can heal the base health, that ability is honestly just useless, and its DPS is way too low. Goes down from high C tier to E tier, now among one of the worst towers. Ace Pilot Ace Pilot’s bombs now aim directly to where its targeted enemy was last at, as opposed to straight down for Levels 2-4 Ace Pilot now has to take off from its runaway, when placed down, and when upgraded to Level 3 and 5. BUG: No longer immune to stuns and freeze. Level 0 Cost: $650 -> $500 Level 2 Splash Damage: 12 -> 10 Explosion Range
